_note: Hand-built atom catalogue for War, modelled on the 'idea atoms' of The Alien Space of Science (arXiv:2603.01092). The released Alien models were NOT used: they are trained on 16,068 LLM research papers, so their atoms are ML-research ideas, not game design. 'commonness' is Claude's judgment (speculation), not measured.

atoms.name: fog of war with remembered last sightings
army-wide morale that ends the battle when it breaks
flank and rear attacks shatter nerve
orders drawn as strokes on the map
spells cast by drawing a glyph
enemy intent shown before it acts
weather front that crosses the field mid-battle
night falls partway through, sight shrinks
terrain that burns, floods or is broken
a river that rises on a clock and drowns fords
a standard-bearer whose banner steadies nearby men
war drums that set the pace of every company in earshot
panic that spreads from a breaking company to its neighbours
broken companies that rally if left alone
veterans and losses that carry between battles
a breaking point that can turn into heroism instead of rout
fatigue from marching and fighting
a column of non-combatants to escort
a duel of champions that sways both armies' nerve
parley and surrender instead of fighting to the last
beaten men who desert, or change sides
orders carried by riders who can be cut down
standing stones that strengthen magic near them
an enemy commander who learns your habits
a named commander with a personal arc told in letters
the battle written up afterward as history
fieldworks dug by sappers during the fight
a pincer: companies arriving from a second edge
a hostage or prisoner to recover
war beasts that terrify horses
feigned retreat that draws pursuers out of formation
scout reports that can be wrong
seasons that change the ground across a campaign
a choice between battles that costs something either way
dead left on the field that block and dishearten
a map that is being drawn as you scout it
ink that runs: orders smudge if the commander's nerve fails
a deterministic replay you can study after defeat

_refs_note: Each reference game stands in for one 'author' in the Alien availability model: a combination is AVAILABLE if some single author already holds most of it. Feature lists are limited to what the cited sources support, plus this repo's own README/PLAN for War.
